messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: manual
parts:
This text from the manual (end of page 30):

Arrays, on the other hand, should be traversed in row-major (or first-index fastest)
order.

Seems to contradict this code:

real a[M,N];

for (m in 1:M)
  for (n in 1:N)
... do something with a[m,n] ...


As well as this text:

The first use of a[m,n] should bring a[m] into memory. Overall, traversing matrices
is more efficient than traversing arrays.

Isn't this last-index-fastest since a[m] (for all values of n) is brought into memory?

Krzysztof

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] manual
parts:
Thanks. I just fixed it for the 2.6 manual.

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1081#issuecomment-71396231

It should say "last-index fastest". I get turned
around easily with signs and directions.

Which is fastest to traverse between array and matrix
depends on which order you go. If you do both optimally,
I'd guess matrices would be a bit faster because the
data structure ensures locality and the arithmetic should
be easily parallelizable by the CPU pipeline.

- Bob
